sections.title: Sec 1: Prerequisite: Understanding Force and Mass
animations: Animation step 1: A white square block (2kg) fades in at center. Label 'm = 2 kg' in #FFFFFF appears above it.
Animation step 2: A red arrow (#FF0000) labeled 'F' slides in from the left, pointing at the block. Label 'F = 10 N' appears next to it.
Animation step 3: The background surface turns a light icy blue (#ADD8E6) to signify 'frictionless'. Text 'Friction = 0' fades in below.
Animation step 4: The red arrow pulses slightly to emphasize the push. The block remains stationary initially.
Animation step 5: A green checkmark (#00FF00) appears next to 'Net Force = F', confirming the simplification.

sections.title: Sec 2: Introducing Newton's Second Law
lecture_lines: Formula: F equals m times a.
animations: Animation step 1: The formula 'F = m * a' appears in the center in large white text (#FFFFFF).
Animation step 2: A small gray block moves slowly to the right. A small red arrow pushes it. Text 'Small F, Low a' appears.
Animation step 3: The red arrow grows larger and brighter. The block moves faster. Text 'Large F, High a' replaces the previous text.
Animation step 4: The block becomes larger (heavier). The same large red arrow is applied, but the block moves slower. Text 'Large m, Low a' appears.
Animation step 5: The variable 'a' in the central formula 'F = m * a' turns yellow (#FFFF00) and scales up slightly to highlight it as the target.

sections.title: Sec 3: Step-by-Step Problem Solving
lecture_lines: Rearrange: a equals F over m.
animations: Animation step 1: Two boxes appear: one labeled 'm = 2 kg' and another 'F = 10 N' in white text on dark gray boxes.
Animation step 2: A question mark '?' appears in a yellow box labeled 'a = ?'. The formula 'F = ma' is shown below.
Animation step 3: The formula animates: 'a' moves to the left, 'm' moves to the denominator. It becomes 'a = F / m'.
Animation step 4: The numbers '10' and '2' slide into the formula. It becomes 'a = 10 / 2'.
Animation step 5: The result '5' flashes in green (#00FF00). The unit 'm/s²' appears next to it. The full equation 'a = 5 m/s²' is highlighted.

sections.title: Sec 4: Real-World Application & Intuition Check
lecture_lines: Zero to 18 km/h in one sec.
animations: Animation step 1: A simple cartoon car icon appears. A speedometer gauge appears next to it.
Animation step 2: The speedometer needle moves rapidly from 0 to a mark labeled '18 km/h'.
Animation step 3: Text '1 second' appears with a timer icon counting down from 1 to 0.
Animation step 4: The car icon moves forward quickly. A green checkmark appears with text 'Reasonable? Yes'.
Animation step 5: The final answer 'a = 5 m/s²' reappears in the center, glowing softly to conclude the lesson.
